question: How many different extras does each airline booking with at least one extra include? Show trip numbers, booking numbers and distinct extra counts for the 10 bookings with the widest variety, largest count first, then by trip number and booking number.
reference_sql: SELECT s~travel_id, s~booking_id, COUNT( DISTINCT s~supplement_id ) AS extra_count FROM /DMO/BOOK_SUPPL AS s GROUP BY s~travel_id, s~booking_id ORDER BY extra_count DESCENDING, s~travel_id ASCENDING, s~booking_id ASCENDING UP TO 10 ROWS

question: For each airline connection scheduled in October 2026, show the airline code and name, connection number, number of scheduled flights, and number of those flights with at least one recorded booking.
reference_sql: SELECT f~carrier_id, c~name, f~connection_id, COUNT( DISTINCT f~flight_date ) AS scheduled_flights, COUNT( DISTINCT b~flight_date ) AS flights_with_bookings FROM /dmo/flight AS f INNER JOIN /dmo/carrier AS c ON c~carrier_id = f~carrier_id LEFT OUTER JOIN /dmo/booking AS b ON b~carrier_id = f~carrier_id AND b~connection_id = f~connection_id AND b~flight_date = f~flight_date WHERE f~flight_date BETWEEN '20261001' AND '20261031' GROUP BY f~carrier_id, c~name, f~connection_id

question: Which combinations of trip currency and flight booking currency occur? Return both currency codes, the number of flight bookings, and the number of distinct trips for each combination.
reference_sql: SELECT t~currency_code AS trip_currency, b~currency_code AS booking_currency, COUNT(*) AS booking_count, COUNT( DISTINCT t~travel_id ) AS trip_count FROM /dmo/travel AS t INNER JOIN /dmo/booking AS b ON b~travel_id = t~travel_id GROUP BY t~currency_code, b~currency_code

question: Which 10 aircraft type and add-on combinations have the most purchased add-on entries? Return aircraft types, add-on codes, and entry counts, most entries first, then alphabetically by aircraft type and add-on code.
reference_sql: SELECT f~plane_type_id, s~supplement_id, COUNT(*) AS entry_count FROM /dmo/book_suppl AS s INNER JOIN /dmo/booking AS b ON b~travel_id = s~travel_id AND b~booking_id = s~booking_id INNER JOIN /dmo/flight AS f ON f~carrier_id = b~carrier_id AND f~connection_id = b~connection_id AND f~flight_date = b~flight_date GROUP BY f~plane_type_id, s~supplement_id ORDER BY entry_count DESCENDING, f~plane_type_id ASCENDING, s~supplement_id ASCENDING UP TO 10 ROWS

question: Which 10 agencies have sold the widest variety of add-ons across their trips? Return agency IDs, names, distinct add-on counts, and purchased entry counts, most distinct add-ons first, then by agency ID.
reference_sql: SELECT a~agency_id, a~name, COUNT( DISTINCT s~supplement_id ) AS addon_count, COUNT(*) AS entry_count FROM /dmo/agency AS a INNER JOIN /dmo/travel AS t ON t~agency_id = a~agency_id INNER JOIN /dmo/book_suppl AS s ON s~travel_id = t~travel_id GROUP BY a~agency_id, a~name ORDER BY addon_count DESCENDING, a~agency_id ASCENDING UP TO 10 ROWS

question: What total distance has been booked with each airline with bookings for listed connections, counting the connection distance once per flight booking? Return airline codes and names, distance units, booking counts, and total distances, separately by distance unit.
reference_sql: SELECT c~carrier_id, c~name, n~distance_unit, COUNT(*) AS booking_count, SUM( n~distance ) AS total_distance FROM /dmo/booking AS b INNER JOIN /dmo/connection AS n ON n~carrier_id = b~carrier_id AND n~connection_id = b~connection_id INNER JOIN /dmo/carrier AS c ON c~carrier_id = b~carrier_id GROUP BY c~carrier_id, c~name, n~distance_unit

question: Which 10 trips have the largest difference between their highest and lowest US-dollar flight booking charges? Return trip IDs, agency names, both charges, and the difference, largest difference first, then by trip ID.
reference_sql: SELECT t~travel_id, a~name, MIN( b~flight_price ) AS lowest_charge, MAX( b~flight_price ) AS highest_charge, MAX( b~flight_price ) - MIN( b~flight_price ) AS charge_difference FROM /dmo/travel AS t INNER JOIN /dmo/agency AS a ON a~agency_id = t~agency_id INNER JOIN /dmo/booking AS b ON b~travel_id = t~travel_id WHERE b~currency_code = 'USD' GROUP BY t~travel_id, a~name ORDER BY charge_difference DESCENDING, t~travel_id ASCENDING UP TO 10 ROWS

question: Which 10 surnames appear on the most customer records? Return surnames, customer counts, and the number of different home countries, most customers first, then alphabetically by surname.
reference_sql: SELECT c~last_name, COUNT(*) AS customer_count, COUNT( DISTINCT c~country_code ) AS country_count FROM /dmo/customer AS c GROUP BY c~last_name ORDER BY customer_count DESCENDING, c~last_name ASCENDING UP TO 10 ROWS

question: Which 10 flight dates have the most unoccupied seats in total? Return dates, flight counts, and total unoccupied seats, most unoccupied seats first, then earliest date.
reference_sql: SELECT f~flight_date, COUNT(*) AS flight_count, SUM( f~seats_max ) - SUM( f~seats_occupied ) AS unoccupied_seats FROM /dmo/flight AS f GROUP BY f~flight_date ORDER BY unoccupied_seats DESCENDING, f~flight_date ASCENDING UP TO 10 ROWS

question: Which 10 airport pairs have the highest total US-dollar flight booking charges, keeping each direction separate? Return departure and arrival airport codes, booking counts, and total charges in dollars, highest total first, then by departure and arrival code.
reference_sql: SELECT n~airport_from_id, n~airport_to_id, COUNT(*) AS booking_count, SUM( b~flight_price ) AS total_charges FROM /dmo/booking AS b INNER JOIN /dmo/connection AS n ON n~carrier_id = b~carrier_id AND n~connection_id = b~connection_id WHERE b~currency_code = 'USD' GROUP BY n~airport_from_id, n~airport_to_id ORDER BY total_charges DESCENDING, n~airport_from_id ASCENDING, n~airport_to_id ASCENDING UP TO 10 ROWS

question: Which 10 airline connections have the largest difference between their highest and lowest occupied-seat counts across scheduled flights? Return airline codes and names, connection numbers, departure and arrival airport codes, both seat counts, and the difference, largest difference first, then by airline code and connection number.
reference_sql: SELECT c~carrier_id, c~name, n~connection_id, n~airport_from_id, n~airport_to_id, MIN( f~seats_occupied ) AS lowest_occupied, MAX( f~seats_occupied ) AS highest_occupied, MAX( f~seats_occupied ) - MIN( f~seats_occupied ) AS seat_difference FROM /dmo/flight AS f INNER JOIN /dmo/connection AS n ON n~carrier_id = f~carrier_id AND n~connection_id = f~connection_id INNER JOIN /dmo/carrier AS c ON c~carrier_id = f~carrier_id GROUP BY c~carrier_id, c~name, n~connection_id, n~airport_from_id, n~airport_to_id ORDER BY seat_difference DESCENDING, c~carrier_id ASCENDING, n~connection_id ASCENDING UP TO 10 ROWS

question: For each trip start date in October 2026, show the number of trips and their total number of flight bookings, including trips without bookings. List dates earliest first.
reference_sql: SELECT t~begin_date, COUNT( DISTINCT t~travel_id ) AS trip_count, COUNT( b~booking_id ) AS booking_count FROM /dmo/travel AS t LEFT OUTER JOIN /dmo/booking AS b ON b~travel_id = t~travel_id WHERE t~begin_date BETWEEN '20261001' AND '20261031' GROUP BY t~begin_date ORDER BY t~begin_date ASCENDING

question: Which 10 flights have bookings from the most different travel agencies? Return airline codes and names, connection numbers, flight dates, and agency counts, most agencies first, then by date, airline code, and connection number.
reference_sql: SELECT b~carrier_id, c~name, b~connection_id, b~flight_date, COUNT( DISTINCT t~agency_id ) AS agency_count FROM /dmo/booking AS b INNER JOIN /dmo/travel AS t ON t~travel_id = b~travel_id INNER JOIN /dmo/carrier AS c ON c~carrier_id = b~carrier_id GROUP BY b~carrier_id, c~name, b~connection_id, b~flight_date ORDER BY agency_count DESCENDING, b~flight_date ASCENDING, b~carrier_id ASCENDING, b~connection_id ASCENDING UP TO 10 ROWS

question: Which 10 airline and add-on category combinations have the most purchased add-on entries? Return airline codes, category codes, entry counts, and distinct passenger counts, most entries first, then by airline code and category code.
reference_sql: SELECT b~carrier_id, s~supplement_category, COUNT(*) AS entry_count, COUNT( DISTINCT b~customer_id ) AS passenger_count FROM /dmo/booking AS b INNER JOIN /dmo/book_suppl AS p ON p~travel_id = b~travel_id AND p~booking_id = b~booking_id INNER JOIN /dmo/supplement AS s ON s~supplement_id = p~supplement_id GROUP BY b~carrier_id, s~supplement_category ORDER BY entry_count DESCENDING, b~carrier_id ASCENDING, s~supplement_category ASCENDING UP TO 10 ROWS

question: Which 10 combinations of departure airport and passenger home country have the most flight bookings? Return airport codes, country codes, booking counts, and distinct passenger counts, most bookings first, then by airport code and country code.
reference_sql: SELECT r~airport_from_id, c~country_code, COUNT(*) AS booking_count, COUNT( DISTINCT b~customer_id ) AS passenger_count FROM /dmo/booking AS b INNER JOIN /dmo/connection AS r ON r~carrier_id = b~carrier_id AND r~connection_id = b~connection_id INNER JOIN /dmo/customer AS c ON c~customer_id = b~customer_id GROUP BY r~airport_from_id, c~country_code ORDER BY booking_count DESCENDING, r~airport_from_id ASCENDING, c~country_code ASCENDING UP TO 10 ROWS

question: For each aircraft type with scheduled flights, show the type and the numbers of different departure airports and arrival airports it serves.
reference_sql: SELECT f~plane_type_id, COUNT( DISTINCT c~airport_from_id ) AS departure_airport_count, COUNT( DISTINCT c~airport_to_id ) AS arrival_airport_count FROM /dmo/flight AS f INNER JOIN /dmo/connection AS c ON c~carrier_id = f~carrier_id AND c~connection_id = f~connection_id GROUP BY f~plane_type_id

question: Which 10 combinations of flight booking date and add-on charge currency have the most purchased add-on entries? Return dates, currencies, entry counts, and total add-on charges in each currency, most entries first, then by date and currency code.
reference_sql: SELECT b~booking_date, p~currency_code, COUNT(*) AS entry_count, SUM( p~price ) AS total_add_on_charges FROM /dmo/booking AS b INNER JOIN /dmo/book_suppl AS p ON p~travel_id = b~travel_id AND p~booking_id = b~booking_id GROUP BY b~booking_date, p~currency_code ORDER BY entry_count DESCENDING, b~booking_date ASCENDING, p~currency_code ASCENDING UP TO 10 ROWS

question: For each agency country and trip status combination with at least one trip, show the country code, status code, number of trips, and number of distinct trip customers.
reference_sql: SELECT a~country_code, t~status, COUNT(*) AS trip_count, COUNT( DISTINCT t~customer_id ) AS customer_count FROM /dmo/agency AS a INNER JOIN /dmo/travel AS t ON t~agency_id = a~agency_id GROUP BY a~country_code, t~status

question: Which 10 passengers made flight bookings on the most different days? Return customer IDs, first and last names, the number of booking days, and their first and last booking dates, most days first, then by customer ID.
reference_sql: SELECT c~customer_id, c~first_name, c~last_name, COUNT( DISTINCT b~booking_date ) AS booking_day_count, MIN( b~booking_date ) AS first_booking_date, MAX( b~booking_date ) AS last_booking_date FROM /dmo/customer AS c INNER JOIN /dmo/booking AS b ON b~customer_id = c~customer_id GROUP BY c~customer_id, c~first_name, c~last_name ORDER BY booking_day_count DESCENDING, c~customer_id ASCENDING UP TO 10 ROWS

question: For each airline with flights booked on trips, what are the lowest and highest trip booking fees among trips containing its flights, separately by trip currency? Return airline codes and names, currencies, both fees, and distinct trip counts.
reference_sql: SELECT c~carrier_id, c~name, t~currency_code, MIN( t~booking_fee ) AS lowest_booking_fee, MAX( t~booking_fee ) AS highest_booking_fee, COUNT( DISTINCT t~travel_id ) AS trip_count FROM /dmo/carrier AS c INNER JOIN /dmo/booking AS b ON b~carrier_id = c~carrier_id INNER JOIN /dmo/travel AS t ON t~travel_id = b~travel_id GROUP BY c~carrier_id, c~name, t~currency_code

question: Which 10 customers have the most different passengers booked across their trips? Return customer IDs, first and last names, and passenger counts, most passengers first, then by customer ID.
reference_sql: SELECT c~customer_id, c~first_name, c~last_name, COUNT( DISTINCT b~customer_id ) AS passenger_count FROM /dmo/customer AS c INNER JOIN /dmo/travel AS t ON t~customer_id = c~customer_id INNER JOIN /dmo/booking AS b ON b~travel_id = t~travel_id GROUP BY c~customer_id, c~first_name, c~last_name ORDER BY passenger_count DESCENDING, c~customer_id ASCENDING UP TO 10 ROWS

question: Which 10 pairs of different add-ons appear together on the most trips? Return both add-on codes and shared trip counts, with the alphabetically earlier code first in each pair. Sort by most trips, then by the first and second codes.
reference_sql: SELECT a~supplement_id AS first_add_on, b~supplement_id AS second_add_on, COUNT( DISTINCT a~travel_id ) AS trip_count FROM /dmo/book_suppl AS a INNER JOIN /dmo/book_suppl AS b ON b~travel_id = a~travel_id AND a~supplement_id < b~supplement_id GROUP BY a~supplement_id, b~supplement_id ORDER BY trip_count DESCENDING, a~supplement_id ASCENDING, b~supplement_id ASCENDING UP TO 10 ROWS

question: Which 10 pairs of airlines share the most departure airports in their listed connections? Return both airline codes and shared airport counts, with the alphabetically earlier airline code first. Sort by most shared airports, then by the first and second airline codes.
reference_sql: SELECT a~carrier_id AS first_airline, b~carrier_id AS second_airline, COUNT( DISTINCT a~airport_from_id ) AS shared_airport_count FROM /dmo/connection AS a INNER JOIN /dmo/connection AS b ON b~airport_from_id = a~airport_from_id AND a~carrier_id < b~carrier_id GROUP BY a~carrier_id, b~carrier_id ORDER BY shared_airport_count DESCENDING, a~carrier_id ASCENDING, b~carrier_id ASCENDING UP TO 10 ROWS

question: Which 10 aircraft type and seating capacity combinations appear on the most scheduled flights? Return aircraft types, seating capacities, and flight counts, most flights first, then by aircraft type and seating capacity.
reference_sql: SELECT f~plane_type_id, f~seats_max, COUNT(*) AS flight_count FROM /dmo/flight AS f GROUP BY f~plane_type_id, f~seats_max ORDER BY flight_count DESCENDING, f~plane_type_id ASCENDING, f~seats_max ASCENDING UP TO 10 ROWS

question: For each country where customers live, show its country code and the numbers of customers and listed travel agencies. Include countries with no agencies.
reference_sql: SELECT c~country_code, COUNT( DISTINCT c~customer_id ) AS customer_count, COUNT( DISTINCT a~agency_id ) AS agency_count FROM /dmo/customer AS c LEFT OUTER JOIN /dmo/agency AS a ON a~country_code = c~country_code GROUP BY c~country_code

question: Which countries have more than 10 customers? Return country codes and customer counts.
reference_sql: SELECT c~country_code, COUNT(*) AS customer_count FROM /dmo/customer AS c GROUP BY c~country_code HAVING COUNT(*) > 10

question: Which currencies are used by at least three airlines? Return currency codes and airline counts.
reference_sql: SELECT c~currency_code, COUNT(*) AS airline_count FROM /dmo/carrier AS c GROUP BY c~currency_code HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3

question: For every catalog add-on, show its code, category code, and the number of languages in which it has a description. Include add-ons without descriptions.
reference_sql: SELECT s~supplement_id, s~supplement_category, COUNT( DISTINCT t~language_code ) AS language_count FROM /dmo/supplement AS s LEFT OUTER JOIN /dmo/suppl_text AS t ON t~supplement_id = s~supplement_id GROUP BY s~supplement_id, s~supplement_category

question: How many customers are recorded under each personal title? Return titles and customer counts, including a group for customers without a title.
reference_sql: SELECT c~title, COUNT(*) AS customer_count FROM /dmo/customer AS c GROUP BY c~title

question: Which 10 trip start and end date combinations are most common? Return both dates and trip counts, most trips first, then by start date and end date.
reference_sql: SELECT t~begin_date, t~end_date, COUNT(*) AS trip_count FROM /dmo/travel AS t GROUP BY t~begin_date, t~end_date ORDER BY trip_count DESCENDING, t~begin_date ASCENDING, t~end_date ASCENDING UP TO 10 ROWS

question: Which 10 passengers have bookings on the most different aircraft types? Return customer IDs, first and last names, and aircraft type counts, most types first, then by customer ID.
reference_sql: SELECT c~customer_id, c~first_name, c~last_name, COUNT( DISTINCT f~plane_type_id ) AS aircraft_type_count FROM /dmo/customer AS c INNER JOIN /dmo/booking AS b ON b~customer_id = c~customer_id INNER JOIN /dmo/flight AS f ON f~carrier_id = b~carrier_id AND f~connection_id = b~connection_id AND f~flight_date = b~flight_date GROUP BY c~customer_id, c~first_name, c~last_name ORDER BY aircraft_type_count DESCENDING, c~customer_id ASCENDING UP TO 10 ROWS

question: For each trip status and departure airport, show the status code, airport code, number of flight bookings, and number of distinct trips containing those bookings.
reference_sql: SELECT t~status, c~airport_from_id, COUNT(*) AS booking_count, COUNT( DISTINCT t~travel_id ) AS trip_count FROM /dmo/travel AS t INNER JOIN /dmo/booking AS b ON b~travel_id = t~travel_id INNER JOIN /dmo/connection AS c ON c~carrier_id = b~carrier_id AND c~connection_id = b~connection_id GROUP BY t~status, c~airport_from_id

question: How many trips were handled by an agency in the same country as the trip customer? Return country codes, trip counts, and distinct customer counts.
reference_sql: SELECT c~country_code, COUNT(*) AS trip_count, COUNT( DISTINCT c~customer_id ) AS customer_count FROM /dmo/travel AS t INNER JOIN /dmo/agency AS a ON a~agency_id = t~agency_id INNER JOIN /dmo/customer AS c ON c~customer_id = t~customer_id WHERE a~country_code = c~country_code GROUP BY c~country_code

question: Which 10 pairs of airlines have the most booked passengers in common? Return both airline codes and shared-passenger counts, with the alphabetically earlier airline code first. Sort by most shared passengers, then by the first and second airline codes.
reference_sql: SELECT b1~carrier_id AS first_airline, b2~carrier_id AS second_airline, COUNT( DISTINCT b1~customer_id ) AS shared_passenger_count FROM /dmo/booking AS b1 INNER JOIN /dmo/booking AS b2 ON b2~customer_id = b1~customer_id AND b1~carrier_id < b2~carrier_id GROUP BY b1~carrier_id, b2~carrier_id ORDER BY shared_passenger_count DESCENDING, first_airline ASCENDING, second_airline ASCENDING UP TO 10 ROWS

question: Which 10 trips include the widest variety of purchased add-on categories? Return trip IDs, agency IDs, category counts, and purchased add-on entry counts, most categories first, then by trip ID.
reference_sql: SELECT t~travel_id, t~agency_id, COUNT( DISTINCT s~supplement_category ) AS category_count, COUNT(*) AS entry_count FROM /dmo/travel AS t INNER JOIN /dmo/book_suppl AS bs ON bs~travel_id = t~travel_id INNER JOIN /dmo/supplement AS s ON s~supplement_id = bs~supplement_id GROUP BY t~travel_id, t~agency_id ORDER BY category_count DESCENDING, t~travel_id ASCENDING UP TO 10 ROWS

question: For each aircraft type, show the number of scheduled flights and occupied seats as a percentage of total seat capacity, rounded to 2 decimals.
reference_sql: SELECT f~plane_type_id, COUNT(*) AS flight_count, DIVISION( SUM( f~seats_occupied ) * 100, SUM( f~seats_max ), 2 ) AS occupancy_percentage FROM /dmo/flight AS f GROUP BY f~plane_type_id

question: For each destination country represented in flight bookings, show its country code, number of distinct passengers, number of flight bookings, and number of different airlines booked.
reference_sql: SELECT a~country, COUNT( DISTINCT b~customer_id ) AS passenger_count, COUNT(*) AS booking_count, COUNT( DISTINCT b~carrier_id ) AS airline_count FROM /dmo/booking AS b INNER JOIN /dmo/connection AS c ON c~carrier_id = b~carrier_id AND c~connection_id = b~connection_id INNER JOIN /dmo/airport AS a ON a~airport_id = c~airport_to_id GROUP BY a~country

question: Which 10 trips have flight bookings for the most distinct passengers? Return trip IDs, agency names, passenger counts, and flight booking counts, most passengers first, then by trip ID.
reference_sql: SELECT t~travel_id, a~name AS agency_name, COUNT( DISTINCT b~customer_id ) AS passenger_count, COUNT(*) AS booking_count FROM /dmo/travel AS t INNER JOIN /dmo/agency AS a ON a~agency_id = t~agency_id INNER JOIN /dmo/booking AS b ON b~travel_id = t~travel_id GROUP BY t~travel_id, a~name ORDER BY passenger_count DESCENDING, t~travel_id ASCENDING UP TO 10 ROWS

question: For each airline with listed connections, show its code and name and how many different departure times and arrival times appear in its timetable.
reference_sql: SELECT a~carrier_id, a~name, COUNT( DISTINCT c~departure_time ) AS departure_time_count, COUNT( DISTINCT c~arrival_time ) AS arrival_time_count FROM /dmo/carrier AS a INNER JOIN /dmo/connection AS c ON c~carrier_id = a~carrier_id GROUP BY a~carrier_id, a~name

question: Show 10 airline and airport-pair combinations where the airline offers connections in both directions. Return airline codes and names and both airport codes, putting the alphabetically earlier airport first. Sort by airline code, then by the first and second airport codes.
reference_sql: SELECT DISTINCT a~carrier_id, a~name, c1~airport_from_id AS first_airport, c1~airport_to_id AS second_airport FROM /dmo/carrier AS a INNER JOIN /dmo/connection AS c1 ON c1~carrier_id = a~carrier_id INNER JOIN /dmo/connection AS c2 ON c2~carrier_id = c1~carrier_id AND c2~airport_from_id = c1~airport_to_id AND c2~airport_to_id = c1~airport_from_id WHERE c1~airport_from_id < c1~airport_to_id ORDER BY a~carrier_id ASCENDING, first_airport ASCENDING, second_airport ASCENDING UP TO 10 ROWS
